newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras explains trade confusion.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras explains trade confusion.

text.p: Brazilian state oil firm Petrobras said $473 million in oil imports failed to be registered in January because of the unfortunate timing of new rules.
Petrobras said in a statement that the fuel was already at sea when the government published a decree December 12 obliging the company to request import permission before loading oil abroad.
"As it stood up to the (end of December), Petrobras could apply for permission to import product up to 90 days after offloading it (in Brazil)," the statement said.
"On (December 17), a decree was published in the Official Journal changing the procedure and obliging Petrobras to ask for import permission before loading abroad.

"At the time the change was announced, Petrobras already had several cargos of gasoline and derivatives at sea, bought on the basis of the old procedure and making it impossible to comply with the new requirement of having to seek prior import permission," it said.
Brazil Thursday announced two trade balances for January after discovering that $473 million worth of oil imports had not been registered in its new Siscomex documentation system.
Not including the unregistered fuel and lubricants, Brazil posted a surprise $60 million trade surplus, the first positive monthly result since last May.
But including the fuel, the result was a $413 million deficit.
Another $120 million worth of Petrobras oil purchases will have to be added to February's imports, officials said.
Petrobras was harshly criticized by officials for failing to adapt to the Siscomex system and for making the government look a fool over the chaos of its January trade figures.
But Petrobras hinted lack of foresight by the government was also to blame.

It said having to register the imports before loading abroad meant setting a fixed destination port, but that the dynamics of the oil business required flexibility in terms of destination and because oil cargo was frequently bought or sold en route.

Petrobras noted the problems had now been resolved with a new decree on January 23 allowing it to request import permission and carry out the registration of imports after offloading the fuel and derivatives in Brazil.
